newsitem.title: USA: Shuffle Master says to beat Q2 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Shuffle Master says to beat Q2 estimates.

text.p: Shuffle Master Inc said Thursday it expects to report net income per share for the second fiscal quarter ended April 30 of $0.13, which would exceed analysts' estimates of $0.09 to $0.11 a share.
John Breeding, Shuffle Master's co-founder and chairman, told analysts at a meeting in Minneapolis that operating earnings would set a new record.
Shuffle Master, which develops and markets products for the casino industry, said it expects to report operating earnings of about $1.9 million. The company will release results next week.
The increase in operating profits is due to continued strength in shuffler system sales, the company said.

"Our preliminary look at the numbers suggests that net income will be about $0.13 per share for the three month period ended April 30, 1997," a statement issued by the company quoted Breeding as saying.

"Shuffle Master has a better financial track record and better growth prospects than at any time in the company's history," Breeding said. He said he has bought Shuffle Master shares in recent months, but the company did not disclose the size of his investment.
